fact: The Minister of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation launched an interim national Cybersecurity Incident Response Team (interim CSIRT) in Maseru on the Wednesday before the 2 August 2026 article (29 July 2026), to serve as the country's command centre for responding to cyber attacks while Parliament works on new laws.
The Oxford GCSCC/C3SA capacity review, final version dated 31 March 2023, states Lesotho has no official National Cybersecurity Strategy and no national CSIRT.

The Acting Principal Secretary of the ICT ministry stated that Government has designated the Lesotho Communications Authority as the interim Computer Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT), ahead of the Cybersecurity Bill; no designation date is given, so the 23 September 2026 publication date is used.

fact: The MICSTI Acting Principal Secretary said the government had designated the Lesotho Communications Authority as the agency for the national Computer Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT), ahead of the Cybersecurity Bill 2026; the article gives no designation date, so the article date is used.

fact: ITWeb Africa reports that Lesotho has launched a National Computer Security Incident Response Team and a National Cybersecurity Forum, with the Ministry of ICT saying the aim is better incident response and coordination; the article gives no event date, so its published date is used.

fact: The Ministry of ICT, with the Lesotho Communications Authority, officially launched the Interim Lesotho National Computer Security Incident Response Team (LesComCSIRT) in Maseru, per the government announcement of 29 July 2026 (published date used, no event date given).
The Ls ComCSIRT, a unit of the Lesotho Communications Authority, was elevated to national status by the Ministry of MICSTI, per its RFC 2350 of March 2026.
